	Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is inviting contractors and suppliers to apply to be placed on an Open Construction Source List (OCSL) for commercial, residential, industrial, institutional, and civil work required by the Department of National Defence, at ASU Chilliwack (including the lower mainland and interior British Columbia) for three fiscal years (April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2029).
	Interested contractors and suppliers may request to be placed on the OCSL at any time. However, DCC is requesting that interested contractors and suppliers submit a request to be placed the OCSL as soon as possible, preferably by March 4, 2026. DCC will require ten (10) business days to process an application for the OCSL.
	Contractors and suppliers that want to be added to the OCSL, must submit a request through this MERX posting and therein indicate their preferred official language (English or French).
	IMPORTANT: Contractors and suppliers that were placed on the previous OCSL (April 1, 2023, to March 31, 2026) must re-apply to be placed on the OCSL for April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2029.
	The language selected by the applicant for this OCSL will be the only language used for the tender documents, the contract documents and communication for all future tenders and during the execution of any resulting contract. The language selected will apply for the duration of the OCSL.
	Faxed, mailed, or emailed submissions will not be accepted. 
	The OCSL will be used to tender construction services (commercial, residential, industrial, institutional, civil) with an estimated value of $10 million and below. As &quot;Opportunities to bid&quot; arise, DCC will invite all contractors and suppliers on the OCSL to bid on the work.
	Contractors and suppliers will be invited electronically through MERX and may, at the discretion of DCC, be required to attend a site meeting prior to a tender closing. Tenders will close electronically through MERX.
	Contractors and suppliers who apply to be placed on the OCSL will require an active MERX account to submit electronic bids. Please contact MERX for information on how to open or reactivate an account.
	To bid on a tender call, a bidder must be registered on the OCSL used for the tender call. If the bidder&#39;s legal name does not appear on the OCSL, DCC may consider their bid to be non-compliant. If you change your business name, it is therefore very important that you notify DCC and consider making the change to your MERX account.
	DCC reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to:
	
		Continue using existing source lists that may already be in place for similar or related services such as existing Quick Response Tender (QRT) source lists,
		Establish other source lists for specific categories of construction services which may require different pre-qualification requirements, such as Quick Response Tender (QRT) source lists. Such other source lists will not be advertised through this OCSL. Such other source lists will be advertised openly on MERX on a case-by-case basis,
		Verify which contractors have submitted bids under the OCSL, verify if those that did not submit bids are still interested to be on the OCSL and remove from the OCSL those contractors that are no longer interested,
		Require additional pre-qualification requirements for any specific tenders done through the OCSL,
		Elect to post any tender openly on MERX in lieu of this OCSL if DCC deems that an open tender would provide the potential for more competition,
		Tenders may be set aside for Indigenous businesses in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). In such cases, all contractors and suppliers on the Open Construction Source List (OCSL) will receive an invitation to bid; however, the MERX advertisement will clearly state that the opportunity is reserved for Indigenous businesses under PSIB. To qualify, the Indigenous business must be registered in Indigenous Services Canada&rsquo;s (ISC) Indigenous Business Directory (IBD). If you are forming a Joint Venture (JV) to bid on a contract set aside for Indigenous businesses, at least one member of the JV must be listed on the OCSL, and the Indigenous business within the JV must also be registered in ISC&rsquo;s Indigenous Business Directory. Failure to meet these requirements will result in the bid being deemed non-compliant,
		Include a requirement for sub-contracting to Indigenous businesses that must be registered under Indigenous Services Canada&rsquo;s (ISC) Indigenous Business Directory. In this case, the MERX Ad specific to the invitation will clearly identify the inclusion of an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP).
	
	
	Contractors are advised that contracts awarded by DCC include measurable performance standards and requirements as detailed in form DCL81-Performance Evaluation Guidelines which is available at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. A contractor that receives an unacceptable or failing score may be removed from this OCSL and receive no further invitations under the OCSL.
	Contractors and suppliers are advised that all contracts tendered and awarded by DCC are subject to DCC&rsquo;s Procurement Code of Conduct which is available for download at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. A contractor or a supplier that has been declared ineligible or has been suspended by Public Services and Procurement Canada under its Ineligibility and Suspension Policy and the period of ineligibility or suspension has not expired may be removed from this OCSL and received no further invitations.
	Contractors and suppliers are advised that DCC&rsquo;s Standard Construction Contract Documents - Electronic Bidding (DCL250) will be used for opportunities under the OCSL and can be downloaded from the DCC website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms.
	Contractors and suppliers are advised that tenders and contracts under this OCSL may contain organization and personnel security requirements. Typically, the organization security requirement will be Designated Organization Screening (DOS) and reliability status for personnel. However more stringent requirement may apply such as Facility Security Clearance (FSC) at the level of SECRET with approved Document Safeguarding (DSC) with secret clearance for personnel.
	DCC may publish Advance Procurement Notices (APN) identifying potential tenders with anticipated security requirements to provide interested contractors an opportunity to begin the sponsorship request process for potentially obtaining the required security clearance(s) that are anticipated. The process to apply for a security clearance is provided in the APNs.
	DCC reserves the right to reject any application that does not demonstrate, to the sole satisfaction of DCC, that the contractor or supplier has met the stated requirements. DCC also reserves the right to request clarifications and/or confirmations from any or all firms regarding any aspect of their submission information. A written response to each such communication is required from the firm.
	By submitting a response to this invitation, contractors and suppliers are providing their consent, pursuant to section 30 of the Defence Production Act, for DCC to publicly disclose, after closing, their legal name, address and whether they have been included on the OCSL.
	The OCSL may be used for procurements covered by trade agreements to which Canada is a party.

	Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is inviting contractors and suppliers to apply to be placed on an Open Construction Source List (OCSL) for commercial, residential, industrial, institutional, and civil work required by the Department of National Defence, at CFB Wainwright for three fiscal years (April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2029).
	Interested contractors and suppliers may request to be placed on the OCSL at any time. However, DCC is requesting that interested contractors and suppliers submit a request to be placed the OCSL as soon as possible, preferably by March 4, 2026. DCC will require ten (10) business days to process an application for the OCSL.
	Contractors and suppliers that want to be added to the OCSL, must submit a request through this MERX posting and therein indicate their preferred official language (English or French).
	IMPORTANT: Contractors and suppliers that were placed on the previous OCSL (April 1, 2023, to March 31, 2026) must re-apply to be placed on the OCSL for April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2029.
	The language selected by the applicant for this OCSL will be the only language used for the tender documents, the contract documents and communication for all future tenders and during the execution of any resulting contract. The language selected will apply for the duration of the OCSL.
	Faxed, mailed, or emailed submissions will not be accepted. 
	The OCSL will be used to tender construction services (commercial, residential, industrial, institutional, civil) with an estimated value of $10 million and below. As &quot;Opportunities to bid&quot; arise, DCC will invite all contractors and suppliers on the OCSL to bid on the work.
	Contractors and suppliers will be invited electronically through MERX and may, at the discretion of DCC, be required to attend a site meeting prior to a tender closing. Tenders will close electronically through MERX.
	Contractors and suppliers who apply to be placed on the OCSL will require an active MERX account to submit electronic bids. Please contact MERX for information on how to open or reactivate an account.
	To bid on a tender call, a bidder must be registered on the OCSL used for the tender call. If the bidder&#39;s legal name does not appear on the OCSL, DCC may consider their bid to be non-compliant. If you change your business name, it is therefore very important that you notify DCC and consider making the change to your MERX account.
	DCC reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to:
	
		Continue using existing source lists that may already be in place for similar or related services such as existing Quick Response Tender (QRT) source lists,
		Establish other source lists for specific categories of construction services which may require different pre-qualification requirements, such as Quick Response Tender (QRT) source lists. Such other source lists will not be advertised through this OCSL. Such other source lists will be advertised openly on MERX on a case-by-case basis,
		Verify which contractors have submitted bids under the OCSL, verify if those that did not submit bids are still interested to be on the OCSL and remove from the OCSL those contractors that are no longer interested,
		Require additional pre-qualification requirements for any specific tenders done through the OCSL,
		Elect to post any tender openly on MERX in lieu of this OCSL if DCC deems that an open tender would provide the potential for more competition,
		Tenders may be set aside for Indigenous businesses in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). In such cases, all contractors and suppliers on the Open Construction Source List (OCSL) will receive an invitation to bid; however, the MERX advertisement will clearly state that the opportunity is reserved for Indigenous businesses under PSIB. To qualify, the Indigenous business must be registered in Indigenous Services Canada&rsquo;s (ISC) Indigenous Business Directory (IBD). If you are forming a Joint Venture (JV) to bid on a contract set aside for Indigenous businesses, at least one member of the JV must be listed on the OCSL, and the Indigenous business within the JV must also be registered in ISC&rsquo;s Indigenous Business Directory. Failure to meet these requirements will result in the bid being deemed non-compliant,
		Include a requirement for sub-contracting to Indigenous businesses that must be registered under Indigenous Services Canada&rsquo;s (ISC) Indigenous Business Directory. In this case, the MERX Ad specific to the invitation will clearly identify the inclusion of an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP).
	
	
	Contractors are advised that contracts awarded by DCC include measurable performance standards and requirements as detailed in form DCL81-Performance Evaluation Guidelines which is available at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. A contractor that receives an unacceptable or failing score may be removed from this OCSL and receive no further invitations under the OCSL.
	Contractors and suppliers are advised that all contracts tendered and awarded by DCC are subject to DCC&rsquo;s Procurement Code of Conduct which is available for download at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. A contractor or a supplier that has been declared ineligible or has been suspended by Public Services and Procurement Canada under its Ineligibility and Suspension Policy and the period of ineligibility or suspension has not expired may be removed from this OCSL and received no further invitations.
	Contractors and suppliers are advised that DCC&rsquo;s Standard Construction Contract Documents - Electronic Bidding (DCL250) will be used for opportunities under the OCSL and can be downloaded from the DCC website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms.
	Contractors and suppliers are advised that tenders and contracts under this OCSL may contain organization and personnel security requirements. Typically, the organization security requirement will be Designated Organization Screening (DOS) and reliability status for personnel. However more stringent requirement may apply such as Facility Security Clearance (FSC) at the level of SECRET with approved Document Safeguarding (DSC) with secret clearance for personnel.
	DCC may publish Advance Procurement Notices (APN) identifying potential tenders with anticipated security requirements to provide interested contractors an opportunity to begin the sponsorship request process for potentially obtaining the required security clearance(s) that are anticipated. The process to apply for a security clearance is provided in the APNs.
	DCC reserves the right to reject any application that does not demonstrate, to the sole satisfaction of DCC, that the contractor or supplier has met the stated requirements. DCC also reserves the right to request clarifications and/or confirmations from any or all firms regarding any aspect of their submission information. A written response to each such communication is required from the firm.
	By submitting a response to this invitation, contractors and suppliers are providing their consent, pursuant to section 30 of the Defence Production Act, for DCC to publicly disclose, after closing, their legal name, address and whether they have been included on the OCSL.
	The OCSL may be used for procurements covered by trade agreements to which Canada is a party.

	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs int&eacute;ress&eacute;s peuvent pr&eacute;senter une demande d&rsquo;adh&eacute;sion au r&eacute;pertoire &agrave; tout moment. Toutefois, CDC demande aux entrepreneurs et fournisseurs int&eacute;ress&eacute;s de soumettre leur demande d&rsquo;adh&eacute;sion au ROEC d&egrave;s que possible, de pr&eacute;f&eacute;rence avant le 4 mars 2026. CDC aura besoins de 10 jours ouvrables pour traiter une demande d&rsquo;adh&eacute;sion au r&eacute;pertoire.
	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs qui d&eacute;sirent adh&eacute;rer au ROEC doivent soumettre leur demande d&rsquo;adh&eacute;sion par le biais de cet affichage MERX et y indiquer leur langue officielle pr&eacute;f&eacute;r&eacute;e (anglais ou Fran&ccedil;ais).
	IMPORTANT&nbsp;: Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs qui figuraient au ROEC pr&eacute;c&eacute;dent (du 1er avril 2023 au 31 mars 2026) doivent pr&eacute;senter une nouvelle demande d&rsquo;adh&eacute;sion au ROEC pour la p&eacute;riode du 1er avril 2026 au 31 mars 2029.
	La langue choisie par le demandeur pour ce r&eacute;pertoire sera la seule langue utilis&eacute;e pour les documents d&rsquo;appel d&rsquo;offres, les documents contractuels et la communication pour toutes les offres futures et pendant l&rsquo;ex&eacute;cution de tout contrat r&eacute;sultant. 	Les demandes d&rsquo;adh&eacute;sion envoy&eacute;es par t&eacute;l&eacute;copieur, par la poste ou par courriel ne seront pas accept&eacute;es.&nbsp;
	Ce ROEC sera utilis&eacute; pour des services de construction (commerciaux, r&eacute;sidentiels, industriels, institutionnels, et de g&eacute;nie civil) d&rsquo;une valeur estim&eacute;e &agrave; 10 millions de dollars et moins. Au fur et &agrave; mesure que des &laquo; occasions de soumissionner &raquo; se pr&eacute;senteront, CDC invitera tous les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs faisant partie du r&eacute;pertoire &agrave; soumissionner pour les travaux.
	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs seront invit&eacute;s par voie &eacute;lectronique par l&rsquo;entremise de MERX et pourront, &agrave; la discr&eacute;tion de CDC, &ecirc;tre tenus d&rsquo;assister &agrave; une r&eacute;union sur place avant la cl&ocirc;ture d&rsquo;un appel d&rsquo;offres.&nbsp; Le d&eacute;p&ocirc;t des soumissions se fera par voie &eacute;lectronique par l&rsquo;entremise de MERX.
	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs qui pr&eacute;sentent une demande d&rsquo;adh&eacute;sion au ROEC auront besoin d&rsquo;un compte MERX actif pour d&eacute;poser des soumissions &eacute;lectroniques. Veuillez communiquer avec MERX pour savoir comment ouvrir ou r&eacute;activer un compte.
	Pour soumissionner dans le cadre d&rsquo;un appel d&rsquo;offres, un soumissionnaire doit &ecirc;tre inscrit sur le ROEC utilis&eacute; pour l&rsquo;appel d&rsquo;offres. Si le nom l&eacute;gal du soumissionnaire n&rsquo;appara&icirc;t pas sur le ROEC, CDC pourrait consid&eacute;rer que sa soumission n&rsquo;est pas conforme. Si vous changez le nom de votre entreprise, il est donc tr&egrave;s important que vous en avisiez CDC et que vous envisagiez &eacute;galement d&rsquo;apporter le changement &agrave; votre compte MERX.

		Mettre en place d&rsquo;autres r&eacute;pertoires pour des cat&eacute;gories sp&eacute;cifiques de services de construction qui peuvent n&eacute;cessiter des exigences de pr&eacute;qualification diff&eacute;rentes, telles que des r&eacute;pertoires pour Soumissions &agrave; Intervention Rapide (SIR). 	Ce ROEC sera utilis&eacute; pour des services de construction (commerciaux, r&eacute;sidentiels, industriels, institutionnels, et de g&eacute;nie civil) d&rsquo;une valeur estim&eacute;e &agrave; 10 millions de dollars et moins. 	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs qui pr&eacute;sentent une demande d&rsquo;adh&eacute;sion au ROEC auront besoin d&rsquo;un compte MERX actif pour d&eacute;poser des soumissions &eacute;lectroniques. Veuillez communiquer avec MERX pour savoir comment ouvrir ou r&eacute;activer un compte.

		Mettre en place d&rsquo;autres r&eacute;pertoires pour des cat&eacute;gories sp&eacute;cifiques de services de construction qui peuvent n&eacute;cessiter des exigences de pr&eacute;qualification diff&eacute;rentes, telles que des r&eacute;pertoires pour Soumissions &agrave; Intervention Rapide (SIR). 		V&eacute;rifiez quels entrepreneurs ont d&eacute;pos&eacute; des soumissions en vertu de ce r&eacute;pertoire, v&eacute;rifiez si ceux qui n&rsquo;ont pas d&eacute;pos&eacute; de soumissions sont toujours int&eacute;ress&eacute;s &agrave; figurer sur le r&eacute;pertoire et retirer du r&eacute;pertoire les entrepreneurs qui ne sont plus int&eacute;ress&eacute;s,

		Inclure une exigence de sous-traitance aux entreprises autochtones qui doivent &ecirc;tre inscrites dans le R&eacute;pertoire des entreprises autochtones de Services aux Autochtones Canada (SAC). 	Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is inviting contractors and suppliers to apply to be placed on an Open Construction Source List (OCSL) for commercial, residential, industrial, institutional, and civil work required by the Department of National Defence, at 4 Wing Cold Lake for three fiscal years (April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2029).
	Interested contractors and suppliers may request to be placed on the OCSL at any time. However, DCC is requesting that interested contractors and suppliers submit a request to be placed the OCSL as soon as possible, preferably by March 4, 2026. DCC will require ten (10) business days to process an application for the OCSL.
	Contractors and suppliers that want to be added to the OCSL, must submit a request through this MERX posting and therein indicate their preferred official language (English or French).
	IMPORTANT: Contractors and suppliers that were placed on the previous OCSL (April 1, 2023, to March 31, 2026) must re-apply to be placed on the OCSL for April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2029.
	The language selected by the applicant for this OCSL will be the only language used for the tender documents, the contract documents and communication for all future tenders and during the execution of any resulting contract. The language selected will apply for the duration of the OCSL.
	Faxed, mailed, or emailed submissions will not be accepted. 
	The OCSL will be used to tender construction services (commercial, residential, industrial, institutional, civil) with an estimated value of $10 million and below. As &quot;Opportunities to bid&quot; arise, DCC will invite all contractors and suppliers on the OCSL to bid on the work.
	Contractors and suppliers will be invited electronically through MERX and may, at the discretion of DCC, be required to attend a site meeting prior to a tender closing. Tenders will close electronically through MERX.
	Contractors and suppliers who apply to be placed on the OCSL will require an active MERX account to submit electronic bids. Please contact MERX for information on how to open or reactivate an account.
	To bid on a tender call, a bidder must be registered on the OCSL used for the tender call. If the bidder&#39;s legal name does not appear on the OCSL, DCC may consider their bid to be non-compliant. If you change your business name, it is therefore very important that you notify DCC and consider making the change to your MERX account.
	DCC reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to:
	
		Continue using existing source lists that may already be in place for similar or related services such as existing Quick Response Tender (QRT) source lists,
		Establish other source lists for specific categories of construction services which may require different pre-qualification requirements, such as Quick Response Tender (QRT) source lists. Such other source lists will not be advertised through this OCSL. Such other source lists will be advertised openly on MERX on a case-by-case basis,
		Verify which contractors have submitted bids under the OCSL, verify if those that did not submit bids are still interested to be on the OCSL and remove from the OCSL those contractors that are no longer interested,
		Require additional pre-qualification requirements for any specific tenders done through the OCSL,
		Elect to post any tender openly on MERX in lieu of this OCSL if DCC deems that an open tender would provide the potential for more competition,
		Tenders may be set aside for Indigenous businesses in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). In such cases, all contractors and suppliers on the Open Construction Source List (OCSL) will receive an invitation to bid; however, the MERX advertisement will clearly state that the opportunity is reserved for Indigenous businesses under PSIB. To qualify, the Indigenous business must be registered in Indigenous Services Canada&rsquo;s (ISC) Indigenous Business Directory (IBD). If you are forming a Joint Venture (JV) to bid on a contract set aside for Indigenous businesses, at least one member of the JV must be listed on the OCSL, and the Indigenous business within the JV must also be registered in ISC&rsquo;s Indigenous Business Directory. Failure to meet these requirements will result in the bid being deemed non-compliant,
		Include a requirement for sub-contracting to Indigenous businesses that must be registered under Indigenous Services Canada&rsquo;s (ISC) Indigenous Business Directory. In this case, the MERX Ad specific to the invitation will clearly identify the inclusion of an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP).

	Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is inviting contractors and suppliers to apply to be placed on an Open Construction Source List (OCSL) for commercial, residential, industrial, institutional, and civil work required by the Department of National Defence, at CFB Calgary (and its satellite sites in Alberta)&nbsp;for three fiscal years (April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2029).
	Interested contractors and suppliers may request to be placed on the OCSL at any time. However, DCC is requesting that interested contractors and suppliers submit a request to be placed the OCSL as soon as possible, preferably by March 4, 2026. DCC will require ten (10) business days to process an application for the OCSL.
	Contractors and suppliers that want to be added to the OCSL, must submit a request through this MERX posting and therein indicate their preferred official language (English or French).
	IMPORTANT: Contractors and suppliers that were placed on the previous OCSL (April 1, 2023, to March 31, 2026) must re-apply to be placed on the OCSL for April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2029.
	The language selected by the applicant for this OCSL will be the only language used for the tender documents, the contract documents and communication for all future tenders and during the execution of any resulting contract. The language selected will apply for the duration of the OCSL.
	Faxed, mailed, or emailed submissions will not be accepted. 
	The OCSL will be used to tender construction services (commercial, residential, industrial, institutional, civil) with an estimated value of $10 million and below. As &quot;Opportunities to bid&quot; arise, DCC will invite all contractors and suppliers on the OCSL to bid on the work.
	Contractors and suppliers will be invited electronically through MERX and may, at the discretion of DCC, be required to attend a site meeting prior to a tender closing. Tenders will close electronically through MERX.
	Contractors and suppliers who apply to be placed on the OCSL will require an active MERX account to submit electronic bids. Please contact MERX for information on how to open or reactivate an account.
	To bid on a tender call, a bidder must be registered on the OCSL used for the tender call. If the bidder&#39;s legal name does not appear on the OCSL, DCC may consider their bid to be non-compliant. If you change your business name, it is therefore very important that you notify DCC and consider making the change to your MERX account.
	DCC reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to:



	Continue using existing source lists that may already be in place for similar or related services such as existing Quick Response Tender (QRT) source lists,
	Establish other source lists for specific categories of construction services which may require different pre-qualification requirements, such as Quick Response Tender (QRT) source lists. Such other source lists will not be advertised through this OCSL. Such other source lists will be advertised openly on MERX on a case-by-case basis,
	Verify which contractors have submitted bids under the OCSL, verify if those that did not submit bids are still interested to be on the OCSL and remove from the OCSL those contractors that are no longer interested,
	Require additional pre-qualification requirements for any specific tenders done through the OCSL,
	Elect to post any tender openly on MERX in lieu of this OCSL if DCC deems that an open tender would provide the potential for more competition,
	Tenders may be set aside for Indigenous businesses in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). In such cases, all contractors and suppliers on the Open Construction Source List (OCSL) will receive an invitation to bid; however, the MERX advertisement will clearly state that the opportunity is reserved for Indigenous businesses under PSIB. To qualify, the Indigenous business must be registered in Indigenous Services Canada&rsquo;s (ISC) Indigenous Business Directory (IBD). If you are forming a Joint Venture (JV) to bid on a contract set aside for Indigenous businesses, at least one member of the JV must be listed on the OCSL, and the Indigenous business within the JV must also be registered in ISC&rsquo;s Indigenous Business Directory. Failure to meet these requirements will result in the bid being deemed non-compliant,
	Include a requirement for sub-contracting to Indigenous businesses that must be registered under Indigenous Services Canada&rsquo;s (ISC) Indigenous Business Directory. In this case, the MERX Ad specific to the invitation will clearly identify the inclusion of an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP).



	Contractors are advised that contracts awarded by DCC include measurable performance standards and requirements as detailed in form DCL81-Performance Evaluation Guidelines which is available at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. A contractor that receives an unacceptable or failing score may be removed from this OCSL and receive no further invitations under the OCSL.
	Contractors and suppliers are advised that all contracts tendered and awarded by DCC are subject to DCC&rsquo;s Procurement Code of Conduct which is available for download at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. A contractor or a supplier that has been declared ineligible or has been suspended by Public Services and Procurement Canada under its Ineligibility and Suspension Policy and the period of ineligibility or suspension has not expired may be removed from this OCSL and received no further invitations.
	Contractors and suppliers are advised that DCC&rsquo;s Standard Construction Contract Documents - Electronic Bidding (DCL250) will be used for opportunities under the OCSL and can be downloaded from the DCC website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms.
	Contractors and suppliers are advised that tenders and contracts under this OCSL may contain organization and personnel security requirements. Typically, the organization security requirement will be Designated Organization Screening (DOS) and reliability status for personnel. However more stringent requirement may apply such as Facility Security Clearance (FSC) at the level of SECRET with approved Document Safeguarding (DSC) with secret clearance for personnel.
	DCC may publish Advance Procurement Notices (APN) identifying potential tenders with anticipated security requirements to provide interested contractors an opportunity to begin the sponsorship request process for potentially obtaining the required security clearance(s) that are anticipated. The process to apply for a security clearance is provided in the APNs.
	DCC reserves the right to reject any application that does not demonstrate, to the sole satisfaction of DCC, that the contractor or supplier has met the stated requirements. DCC also reserves the right to request clarifications and/or confirmations from any or all firms regarding any aspect of their submission information. A written response to each such communication is required from the firm.
	By submitting a response to this invitation, contractors and suppliers are providing their consent, pursuant to section 30 of the Defence Production Act, for DCC to publicly disclose, after closing, their legal name, address and whether they have been included on the OCSL.
	The OCSL may be used for procurements covered by trade agreements to which Canada is a party.

	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs qui d&eacute;sirent adh&eacute;rer au ROEC doivent soumettre leur demande d&rsquo;adh&eacute;sion par le biais de cet affichage MERX et y indiquer leur langue officielle pr&eacute;f&eacute;r&eacute;e (anglais ou Fran&ccedil;ais).

	La langue choisie par le demandeur pour ce r&eacute;pertoire sera la seule langue utilis&eacute;e pour les documents d&rsquo;appel d&rsquo;offres, les documents contractuels et la communication pour toutes les offres futures et pendant l&rsquo;ex&eacute;cution de tout contrat r&eacute;sultant. 	Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is inviting contractors and suppliers to apply to be placed on an Open Construction Source List (OCSL) for commercial, residential, industrial, institutional, and civil work required by the Department of National Defence, at CFB Shilo for three fiscal years (April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2029)
	Interested contractors and suppliers may request to be placed on the OCSL at any time. However, DCC is requesting that interested contractors and suppliers submit a request to be placed the OCSL as soon as possible, preferably by March 4, 2026. DCC will require ten (10) business days to process an application for the OCSL.
	Contractors and suppliers that want to be added to the OCSL, must submit a request through this MERX posting and therein indicate their preferred official language (English or French).
	IMPORTANT: Contractors and suppliers that were placed on the previous OCSL (April 1, 2023, to March 31, 2026) must re-apply to be placed on the OCSL for April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2029.
	The language selected by the applicant for this OCSL will be the only language used for the tender documents, the contract documents and communication for all future tenders and during the execution of any resulting contract. The language selected will apply for the duration of the OCSL.
	Faxed, mailed, or emailed submissions will not be accepted. 
	The OCSL will be used to tender construction services (commercial, residential, industrial, institutional, civil) with an estimated value of $10 million and below. As &quot;Opportunities to bid&quot; arise, DCC will invite all contractors and suppliers on the OCSL to bid on the work.
	Contractors and suppliers will be invited electronically through MERX and may, at the discretion of DCC, be required to attend a site meeting prior to a tender closing. Tenders will close electronically through MERX.
	Contractors and suppliers who apply to be placed on the OCSL will require an active MERX account to submit electronic bids. Please contact MERX for information on how to open or reactivate an account.
	To bid on a tender call, a bidder must be registered on the OCSL used for the tender call. If the bidder&#39;s legal name does not appear on the OCSL, DCC may consider their bid to be non-compliant. If you change your business name, it is therefore very important that you notify DCC and consider making the change to your MERX account.
	DCC reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to:
	
		Continue using existing source lists that may already be in place for similar or related services such as existing Quick Response Tender (QRT) source lists,
		Establish other source lists for specific categories of construction services which may require different pre-qualification requirements, such as Quick Response Tender (QRT) source lists. Such other source lists will not be advertised through this OCSL. Such other source lists will be advertised openly on MERX on a case-by-case basis,
		Verify which contractors have submitted bids under the OCSL, verify if those that did not submit bids are still interested to be on the OCSL and remove from the OCSL those contractors that are no longer interested,
		Require additional pre-qualification requirements for any specific tenders done through the OCSL,
		Elect to post any tender openly on MERX in lieu of this OCSL if DCC deems that an open tender would provide the potential for more competition,
		Tenders may be set aside for Indigenous businesses in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). In such cases, all contractors and suppliers on the Open Construction Source List (OCSL) will receive an invitation to bid; however, the MERX advertisement will clearly state that the opportunity is reserved for Indigenous businesses under PSIB. To qualify, the Indigenous business must be registered in Indigenous Services Canada&rsquo;s (ISC) Indigenous Business Directory (IBD). If you are forming a Joint Venture (JV) to bid on a contract set aside for Indigenous businesses, at least one member of the JV must be listed on the OCSL, and the Indigenous business within the JV must also be registered in ISC&rsquo;s Indigenous Business Directory. Failure to meet these requirements will result in the bid being deemed non-compliant,
		Include a requirement for sub-contracting to Indigenous businesses that must be registered under Indigenous Services Canada&rsquo;s (ISC) Indigenous Business Directory. 	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs qui d&eacute;sirent adh&eacute;rer au ROEC doivent soumettre leur demande d&rsquo;adh&eacute;sion par le biais de cet affichage MERX et y indiquer leur langue officielle pr&eacute;f&eacute;r&eacute;e (anglais ou Fran&ccedil;ais).

	La langue choisie par le demandeur pour ce r&eacute;pertoire sera la seule langue utilis&eacute;e pour les documents d&rsquo;appel d&rsquo;offres, les documents contractuels et la communication pour toutes les offres futures et pendant l&rsquo;ex&eacute;cution de tout contrat r&eacute;sultant. Au fur et &agrave; mesure que des &laquo; occasions de soumissionner &raquo; se pr&eacute;senteront, CDC invitera tous les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs faisant partie du r&eacute;pertoire &agrave; soumissionner pour les travaux.
	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs seront invit&eacute;s par voie &eacute;lectronique par l&rsquo;entremise de MERX et pourront, &agrave; la discr&eacute;tion de CDC, &ecirc;tre tenus d&rsquo;assister &agrave; une r&eacute;union sur place avant la cl&ocirc;ture d&rsquo;un appel d&rsquo;offres.&nbsp; Le d&eacute;p&ocirc;t des soumissions se fera par voie &eacute;lectronique par l&rsquo;entremise de MERX.
	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs qui pr&eacute;sentent une demande d&rsquo;adh&eacute;sion au ROEC auront besoin d&rsquo;un compte MERX actif pour d&eacute;poser des soumissions &eacute;lectroniques. Veuillez communiquer avec MERX pour savoir comment ouvrir ou r&eacute;activer un compte.
	Pour soumissionner dans le cadre d&rsquo;un appel d&rsquo;offres, un soumissionnaire doit &ecirc;tre inscrit sur le ROEC utilis&eacute; pour l&rsquo;appel d&rsquo;offres. Si le nom l&eacute;gal du soumissionnaire n&rsquo;appara&icirc;t pas sur le ROEC, CDC pourrait consid&eacute;rer que sa soumission n&rsquo;est pas conforme. Si vous changez le nom de votre entreprise, il est donc tr&egrave;s important que vous en avisiez CDC et que vous envisagiez &eacute;galement d&rsquo;apporter le changement &agrave; votre compte MERX.

		Continuer &agrave; utiliser les r&eacute;pertoires d&eacute;j&agrave; en place pour des services similaires ou connexes, tels que les r&eacute;pertoires pour Soumissions &agrave; Intervention Rapide (SIR),
		Mettre en place d&rsquo;autres r&eacute;pertoires pour des cat&eacute;gories sp&eacute;cifiques de services de construction qui peuvent n&eacute;cessiter des exigences de pr&eacute;qualification diff&eacute;rentes, telles que des r&eacute;pertoires pour Soumissions &agrave; Intervention Rapide (SIR). 		V&eacute;rifiez quels entrepreneurs ont d&eacute;pos&eacute; des soumissions en vertu de ce r&eacute;pertoire, v&eacute;rifiez si ceux qui n&rsquo;ont pas d&eacute;pos&eacute; de soumissions sont toujours int&eacute;ress&eacute;s &agrave; figurer sur le r&eacute;pertoire et retirer du r&eacute;pertoire les entrepreneurs qui ne sont plus int&eacute;ress&eacute;s,

		Inclure une exigence de sous-traitance aux entreprises autochtones qui doivent &ecirc;tre inscrites dans le R&eacute;pertoire des entreprises autochtones de Services aux Autochtones Canada (SAC). Au fur et &agrave; mesure que des &laquo; occasions de soumissionner &raquo; se pr&eacute;senteront, CDC invitera tous les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs faisant partie du r&eacute;pertoire &agrave; soumissionner pour les travaux.
	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs seront invit&eacute;s par voie &eacute;lectronique par l&rsquo;entremise de MERX et pourront, &agrave; la discr&eacute;tion de CDC, &ecirc;tre tenus d&rsquo;assister &agrave; une r&eacute;union sur place avant la cl&ocirc;ture d&rsquo;un appel d&rsquo;offres.&nbsp; Le d&eacute;p&ocirc;t des soumissions se fera par voie &eacute;lectronique par l&rsquo;entremise de MERX.
	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs qui pr&eacute;sentent une demande d&rsquo;adh&eacute;sion au ROEC auront besoin d&rsquo;un compte MERX actif pour d&eacute;poser des soumissions &eacute;lectroniques. Veuillez communiquer avec MERX pour savoir comment ouvrir ou r&eacute;activer un compte.
	Pour soumissionner dans le cadre d&rsquo;un appel d&rsquo;offres, un soumissionnaire doit &ecirc;tre inscrit sur le ROEC utilis&eacute; pour l&rsquo;appel d&rsquo;offres. Si le nom l&eacute;gal du soumissionnaire n&rsquo;appara&icirc;t pas sur le ROEC, CDC pourrait consid&eacute;rer que sa soumission n&rsquo;est pas conforme. Si vous changez le nom de votre entreprise, il est donc tr&egrave;s important que vous en avisiez CDC et que vous envisagiez &eacute;galement d&rsquo;apporter le changement &agrave; votre compte MERX.
	CDC se r&eacute;serve le droit, &agrave; sa seule discr&eacute;tion, de :
	
		Continuer &agrave; utiliser les r&eacute;pertoires d&eacute;j&agrave; en place pour des services similaires ou connexes, tels que les r&eacute;pertoires pour Soumissions &agrave; Intervention Rapide (SIR),
		Mettre en place d&rsquo;autres r&eacute;pertoires pour des cat&eacute;gories sp&eacute;cifiques de services de construction qui peuvent n&eacute;cessiter des exigences de pr&eacute;qualification diff&eacute;rentes, telles que des r&eacute;pertoires pour Soumissions &agrave; Intervention Rapide (SIR). Ces autres r&eacute;pertoires ne seront pas annonc&eacute;s par le biais de ce r&eacute;pertoire. Ces autres r&eacute;pertoires seront annonc&eacute;s ouvertement sur MERX au cas par cas,
		V&eacute;rifiez quels entrepreneurs ont d&eacute;pos&eacute; des soumissions en vertu de ce r&eacute;pertoire, v&eacute;rifiez si ceux qui n&rsquo;ont pas d&eacute;pos&eacute; de soumissions sont toujours int&eacute;ress&eacute;s &agrave; figurer sur le r&eacute;pertoire et retirer du r&eacute;pertoire les entrepreneurs qui ne sont plus int&eacute;ress&eacute;s,
		Exiger des besoins de pr&eacute;qualification suppl&eacute;mentaires pour toute soumission sp&eacute;cifique effectu&eacute;e par l&rsquo;interm&eacute;diaire du r&eacute;pertoire,
		Choisir d&rsquo;afficher ouvertement tout appel d&rsquo;offres sur MERX au lieu d&rsquo;utiliser le r&eacute;pertoire si CDC estime qu&rsquo;un appel d&rsquo;offres ouvert pourrait accro&icirc;tre la concurrence,
		R&eacute;server des appels d&rsquo;offres aux entreprises autochtones conform&eacute;ment &agrave; la Strat&eacute;gie d&rsquo;approvisionnement aupr&egrave;s des entreprises autochtones (SAEA). Dans ce cas, tous les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs inscrits au R&eacute;pertoire ouvert d&rsquo;entrepreneurs en construction (ROEC) recevront une invitation &agrave; soumissionner; toutefois, l&rsquo;annonce publi&eacute;e sur MERX indiquera clairement que l&rsquo;occasion est r&eacute;serv&eacute;e aux entreprises autochtones en vertu de la SAEA. Pour &ecirc;tre admissible, l&rsquo;entreprise autochtone doit &ecirc;tre inscrite au R&eacute;pertoire des entreprises autochtones (REA) de Services aux Autochtones Canada (SAC). Si vous formez une coentreprise (JV) pour soumissionner sur un contrat r&eacute;serv&eacute; aux entreprises autochtones, au moins un membre de la coentreprise doit figurer au ROEC, et l&rsquo;entreprise autochtone faisant partie de la coentreprise doit &eacute;galement &ecirc;tre inscrite au R&eacute;pertoire des entreprises autochtones de SAC. Le non-respect de ces exigences entra&icirc;nera le rejet de la soumission pour non-conformit&eacute;,
		Inclure une exigence de sous-traitance aux entreprises autochtones qui doivent &ecirc;tre inscrites dans le R&eacute;pertoire des entreprises autochtones de Services aux Autochtones Canada (SAC). Dans ce cas, l&rsquo;annonce MERX sp&eacute;cifique &agrave; l&rsquo;invitation indiquera clairement l&rsquo;inclusion d&rsquo;un volet de participation aux Autochtones.
	
	
	Les entrepreneurs sont avis&eacute;s que les contrats mis en place par CDC comprennent des normes et des exigences de rendement mesurables, comme indiqu&eacute; dans le formulaire CDL81 - Lignes directrices sur l&rsquo;&eacute;valuation du rendement, disponible &agrave; https://www.cdc-dcc.gc.ca/industrie/formulaires. Un entrepreneur qui re&ccedil;oit une note inacceptable ou une mention d&rsquo;&eacute;chec peut &ecirc;tre retir&eacute; de ce r&eacute;pertoire et ne recevoir aucune autre invitation en vertu de ce r&eacute;pertoire.
	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs sont avis&eacute;s que tous les appels d&rsquo;offres et les contrats mis en place par CDC sont assujettis au Code de conduite en mati&egrave;re d&rsquo;approvisionnement de CDC, qui peut &ecirc;tre t&eacute;l&eacute;charg&eacute; &agrave; l&rsquo;adresse https://www.cdc-dcc.gc.ca/industrie/formulaires. Un entrepreneur ou un fournisseur qui a &eacute;t&eacute; d&eacute;clar&eacute; inadmissible ou qui a &eacute;t&eacute; suspendu par Services publics et Approvisionnement Canada en vertu de sa Politique d&rsquo;inadmissibilit&eacute; et de suspension et dont la p&eacute;riode d&rsquo;inadmissibilit&eacute; ou de suspension n&rsquo;a pas expir&eacute; peut &ecirc;tre retir&eacute; du r&eacute;pertoire et ne recevoir aucune autre invitation.
	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs sont avis&eacute;s que les Documents de contrat de construction standards pour soumissions &eacute;lectroniques de CDC (CDL250) seront utilis&eacute;s pour les opportunit&eacute;s en vertu de ce r&eacute;pertoire et peuvent &ecirc;tre t&eacute;l&eacute;charg&eacute;s &agrave; partir du site Web de CDC &agrave; l&rsquo;adresse suivante : https://www.cdc-dcc.gc.ca/industrie/formulaires.
	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs sont avis&eacute;s que les appels d&rsquo;offres et les contrats en vertu du pr&eacute;sent r&eacute;pertoire peuvent contenir des exigences en mati&egrave;re de s&eacute;curit&eacute; de l&rsquo;organisation et de s&eacute;curit&eacute; du personnel.&nbsp; En r&egrave;gle g&eacute;n&eacute;rale, l&rsquo;exigence de s&eacute;curit&eacute; de l&rsquo;organisation sera la v&eacute;rification de l&rsquo;organisation d&eacute;sign&eacute;e (VOD) et la cote de fiabilit&eacute; pour le personnel. 	CDC se r&eacute;serve le droit de rejeter toute demande de pr&eacute;qualification qui ne d&eacute;montre pas, &agrave; la seule satisfaction de CDC, que l&rsquo;entrepreneur a satisfait aux exigences &eacute;nonc&eacute;es.&nbsp; CDC se r&eacute;serve &eacute;galement le droit de demander des &eacute;claircissements ou des confirmations &agrave; l&rsquo;un ou &agrave; l&rsquo;ensemble des entrepreneurs concernant tout aspect des renseignements qu&rsquo;ils soumettent. 	Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is inviting contractors and suppliers to apply to be placed on an Open Construction Source List (OCSL) for commercial, residential, industrial, institutional, and civil work required by the Department of National Defence, at CFB Edmonton for three fiscal years (April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2029).
	Interested contractors and suppliers may request to be placed on the OCSL at any time. However, DCC is requesting that interested contractors and suppliers submit a request to be placed the OCSL as soon as possible, preferably by March 4, 2026. DCC will require ten (10) business days to process an application for the OCSL.
	Contractors and suppliers that want to be added to the OCSL, must submit a request through this MERX posting and therein indicate their preferred official language (English or French).
	IMPORTANT: Contractors and suppliers that were placed on the previous OCSL (April 1, 2023, to March 31, 2026) must re-apply to be placed on the OCSL for April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2029.
	The language selected by the applicant for this OCSL will be the only language used for the tender documents, the contract documents and communication for all future tenders and during the execution of any resulting contract. The language selected will apply for the duration of the OCSL.
	Faxed, mailed, or emailed submissions will not be accepted. 
	The OCSL will be used to tender construction services (commercial, residential, industrial, institutional, civil) with an estimated value of $10 million and below. As &quot;Opportunities to bid&quot; arise, DCC will invite all contractors and suppliers on the OCSL to bid on the work.
	Contractors and suppliers will be invited electronically through MERX and may, at the discretion of DCC, be required to attend a site meeting prior to a tender closing. Tenders will close electronically through MERX.
	Contractors and suppliers who apply to be placed on the OCSL will require an active MERX account to submit electronic bids. Please contact MERX for information on how to open or reactivate an account.
	To bid on a tender call, a bidder must be registered on the OCSL used for the tender call. If the bidder&#39;s legal name does not appear on the OCSL, DCC may consider their bid to be non-compliant. If you change your business name, it is therefore very important that you notify DCC and consider making the change to your MERX account.
	DCC reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to:
	
		Continue using existing source lists that may already be in place for similar or related services such as existing Quick Response Tender (QRT) source lists,
		Establish other source lists for specific categories of construction services which may require different pre-qualification requirements, such as Quick Response Tender (QRT) source lists. Such other source lists will not be advertised through this OCSL. Such other source lists will be advertised openly on MERX on a case-by-case basis,
		Verify which contractors have submitted bids under the OCSL, verify if those that did not submit bids are still interested to be on the OCSL and remove from the OCSL those contractors that are no longer interested,
		Require additional pre-qualification requirements for any specific tenders done through the OCSL,
		Elect to post any tender openly on MERX in lieu of this OCSL if DCC deems that an open tender would provide the potential for more competition,
		Tenders may be set aside for Indigenous businesses in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). In such cases, all contractors and suppliers on the Open Construction Source List (OCSL) will receive an invitation to bid; however, the MERX advertisement will clearly state that the opportunity is reserved for Indigenous businesses under PSIB. To qualify, the Indigenous business must be registered in Indigenous Services Canada&rsquo;s (ISC) Indigenous Business Directory (IBD). If you are forming a Joint Venture (JV) to bid on a contract set aside for Indigenous businesses, at least one member of the JV must be listed on the OCSL, and the Indigenous business within the JV must also be registered in ISC&rsquo;s Indigenous Business Directory. Failure to meet these requirements will result in the bid being deemed non-compliant,
		Include a requirement for sub-contracting to Indigenous businesses that must be registered under Indigenous Services Canada&rsquo;s (ISC) Indigenous Business Directory. In this case, the MERX Ad specific to the invitation will clearly identify the inclusion of an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP).
	
	
	Contractors are advised that contracts awarded by DCC include measurable performance standards and requirements as detailed in form DCL81-Performance Evaluation Guidelines which is available at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. A contractor that receives an unacceptable or failing score may be removed from this OCSL and receive no further invitations under the OCSL.
	Contractors and suppliers are advised that all contracts tendered and awarded by DCC are subject to DCC&rsquo;s Procurement Code of Conduct which is available for download at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. A contractor or a supplier that has been declared ineligible or has been suspended by Public Services and Procurement Canada under its Ineligibility and Suspension Policy and the period of ineligibility or suspension has not expired may be removed from this OCSL and received no further invitations.
	Contractors and suppliers are advised that DCC&rsquo;s Standard Construction Contract Documents - Electronic Bidding (DCL250) will be used for opportunities under the OCSL and can be downloaded from the DCC website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms.
	Contractors and suppliers are advised that tenders and contracts under this OCSL may contain organization and personnel security requirements. Typically, the organization security requirement will be Designated Organization Screening (DOS) and reliability status for personnel. However more stringent requirement may apply such as Facility Security Clearance (FSC) at the level of SECRET with approved Document Safeguarding (DSC) with secret clearance for personnel.
	DCC may publish Advance Procurement Notices (APN) identifying potential tenders with anticipated security requirements to provide interested contractors an opportunity to begin the sponsorship request process for potentially obtaining the required security clearance(s) that are anticipated. The process to apply for a security clearance is provided in the APNs.
	DCC reserves the right to reject any application that does not demonstrate, to the sole satisfaction of DCC, that the contractor or supplier has met the stated requirements. DCC also reserves the right to request clarifications and/or confirmations from any or all firms regarding any aspect of their submission information. A written response to each such communication is required from the firm.
	By submitting a response to this invitation, contractors and suppliers are providing their consent, pursuant to section 30 of the Defence Production Act, for DCC to publicly disclose, after closing, their legal name, address and whether they have been included on the OCSL.
	The OCSL may be used for procurements covered by trade agreements to which Canada is a party.

	Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is inviting contractors and suppliers to apply to be placed on an Open Construction Source List (OCSL) for commercial, residential, industrial, institutional, and civil work required by the Department of National Defence, in the National Capital Region (Ottawa and Gatineau) for three fiscal years (April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2029).
	Interested contractors and suppliers may request to be placed on the OCSL at any time. However, DCC is requesting that interested contractors and suppliers submit a request to be placed the OCSL as soon as possible, preferably by March 4, 2026. DCC will require ten (10) business days to process an application for the OCSL.
	Contractors and suppliers that want to be added to the OCSL, must submit a request through this MERX posting and therein indicate their preferred official language (English or French).
	IMPORTANT: Contractors and suppliers that were placed on the previous OCSL (April 1, 2023, to March 31, 2026) must re-apply to be placed on the OCSL for April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2029.
	The language selected by the applicant for this OCSL will be the only language used for the tender documents, the contract documents and communication for all future tenders and during the execution of any resulting contract. The language selected will apply for the duration of the OCSL.
	Faxed, mailed, or emailed submissions will not be accepted. 
	The OCSL will be used to tender construction services (commercial, residential, industrial, institutional, civil) with an estimated value of $10 million and below. As &quot;Opportunities to bid&quot; arise, DCC will invite all contractors and suppliers on the OCSL to bid on the work.
	Contractors and suppliers will be invited electronically through MERX and may, at the discretion of DCC, be required to attend a site meeting prior to a tender closing. Tenders will close electronically through MERX.
	Contractors and suppliers who apply to be placed on the OCSL will require an active MERX account to submit electronic bids. Please contact MERX for information on how to open or reactivate an account.
	To bid on a tender call, a bidder must be registered on the OCSL used for the tender call. If the bidder&#39;s legal name does not appear on the OCSL, DCC may consider their bid to be non-compliant. If you change your business name, it is therefore very important that you notify DCC and consider making the change to your MERX account.
	DCC reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to:
	
		Continue using existing source lists that may already be in place for similar or related services such as existing Quick Response Tender (QRT) source lists,
		Establish other source lists for specific categories of construction services which may require different pre-qualification requirements, such as Quick Response Tender (QRT) source lists. Such other source lists will not be advertised through this OCSL. Such other source lists will be advertised openly on MERX on a case-by-case basis,
		Verify which contractors have submitted bids under the OCSL, verify if those that did not submit bids are still interested to be on the OCSL and remove from the OCSL those contractors that are no longer interested,
		Require additional pre-qualification requirements for any specific tenders done through the OCSL,
		Elect to post any tender openly on MERX in lieu of this OCSL if DCC deems that an open tender would provide the potential for more competition,
		Tenders may be set aside for Indigenous businesses in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). In such cases, all contractors and suppliers on the Open Construction Source List (OCSL) will receive an invitation to bid; however, the MERX advertisement will clearly state that the opportunity is reserved for Indigenous businesses under PSIB. To qualify, the Indigenous business must be registered in Indigenous Services Canada&rsquo;s (ISC) Indigenous Business Directory (IBD). If you are forming a Joint Venture (JV) to bid on a contract set aside for Indigenous businesses, at least one member of the JV must be listed on the OCSL, and the Indigenous business within the JV must also be registered in ISC&rsquo;s Indigenous Business Directory. Failure to meet these requirements will result in the bid being deemed non-compliant,
		Include a requirement for sub-contracting to Indigenous businesses that must be registered under Indigenous Services Canada&rsquo;s (ISC) Indigenous Business Directory. In this case, the MERX Ad specific to the invitation will clearly identify the inclusion of an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP).

	Contractors and suppliers are advised that all contracts tendered and awarded by DCC are subject to DCC&rsquo;s Procurement Code of Conduct which is available for download at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. A contractor or a supplier that has been declared ineligible or has been suspended by Public Services and Procurement Canada under its Ineligibility and Suspension Policy and the period of ineligibility or suspension has not expired may be removed from this OCSL and received no further invitations.
	Contractors and suppliers are advised that DCC&rsquo;s Standard Construction Contract Documents - Electronic Bidding (DCL250) will be used for opportunities under the OCSL and can be downloaded from the DCC website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms.
	Contractors and suppliers are advised that tenders and contracts under this OCSL may contain organization and personnel security requirements. 	DCC may publish Advance Procurement Notices (APN) identifying potential tenders with anticipated security requirements to provide interested contractors an opportunity to begin the sponsorship request process for potentially obtaining the required security clearance(s) that are anticipated. 	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs int&eacute;ress&eacute;s peuvent pr&eacute;senter une demande d&rsquo;adh&eacute;sion au r&eacute;pertoire &agrave; tout moment. Toutefois, CDC demande aux entrepreneurs et fournisseurs int&eacute;ress&eacute;s de soumettre leur demande d&rsquo;adh&eacute;sion au ROEC d&egrave;s que possible, de pr&eacute;f&eacute;rence avant le 4 mars 2026. CDC aura besoins de 10 jours ouvrables pour traiter une demande d&rsquo;adh&eacute;sion au r&eacute;pertoire.
	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs qui d&eacute;sirent adh&eacute;rer au ROEC doivent soumettre leur demande d&rsquo;adh&eacute;sion par le biais de cet affichage MERX et y indiquer leur langue officielle pr&eacute;f&eacute;r&eacute;e (anglais ou Fran&ccedil;ais).
	IMPORTANT&nbsp;: Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs qui figuraient au ROEC pr&eacute;c&eacute;dent (du 1er avril 2023 au 31 mars 2026) doivent pr&eacute;senter une nouvelle demande d&rsquo;adh&eacute;sion au ROEC pour la p&eacute;riode du 1er avril 2026 au 31 mars 2029.
	La langue choisie par le demandeur pour ce r&eacute;pertoire sera la seule langue utilis&eacute;e pour les documents d&rsquo;appel d&rsquo;offres, les documents contractuels et la communication pour toutes les offres futures et pendant l&rsquo;ex&eacute;cution de tout contrat r&eacute;sultant. 	Les demandes d&rsquo;adh&eacute;sion envoy&eacute;es par t&eacute;l&eacute;copieur, par la poste ou par courriel ne seront pas accept&eacute;es.&nbsp;
	Ce ROEC sera utilis&eacute; pour des services de construction (commerciaux, r&eacute;sidentiels, industriels, institutionnels, et de g&eacute;nie civil) d&rsquo;une valeur estim&eacute;e &agrave; 10 millions de dollars et moins. Au fur et &agrave; mesure que des &laquo; occasions de soumissionner &raquo; se pr&eacute;senteront, CDC invitera tous les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs faisant partie du r&eacute;pertoire &agrave; soumissionner pour les travaux.
	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs seront invit&eacute;s par voie &eacute;lectronique par l&rsquo;entremise de MERX et pourront, &agrave; la discr&eacute;tion de CDC, &ecirc;tre tenus d&rsquo;assister &agrave; une r&eacute;union sur place avant la cl&ocirc;ture d&rsquo;un appel d&rsquo;offres.&nbsp; Le d&eacute;p&ocirc;t des soumissions se fera par voie &eacute;lectronique par l&rsquo;entremise de MERX.
	Les entrepreneurs et fournisseurs qui pr&eacute;sentent une demande d&rsquo;adh&eacute;sion au ROEC auront besoin d&rsquo;un compte MERX actif pour d&eacute;poser des soumissions &eacute;lectroniques. Veuillez communiquer avec MERX pour savoir comment ouvrir ou r&eacute;activer un compte.

Si le nom l&eacute;gal du soumissionnaire n&rsquo;appara&icirc;t pas sur le ROEC, CDC pourrait consid&eacute;rer que sa soumission n&rsquo;est pas conforme. 1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE
This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals.

In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform consultants of an upcoming contract opportunity at various locations in British Columbia.

The purpose of this APN is to allow consultants to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process.

This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested [contractors and consultants] to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable).

Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process.

2. DESCRIPTION OF THE Standing Offer Agreement AND SERVICES
It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND.

APN Number:88336
Approximate Estimate: $1,000,000
Anticipated Posting: Winter 2027

Description:
It is the Department of National Defence/Canadian Armed Forces (DND/CAF) policy to maintain a General Safety Program (GSP), which ensures that safety considerations are incorporated into every aspect of departmental operations, training, and support activities. The Consultant will be responsible to maintain (if necessary) and deliver training courses on an as needed basis to DND/CAF in the courses falling within a General Safety training category. Safety training courses that may be requested to be delivered by the Consultant include: confined space entry and rescue; fall arrest equipment inspection; first aid training, and asbestos and lead procedures.
The estimated total potential opportunity is approximately $1,000,000 over the 5-year period.

3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS

The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS).

1. OBJECTIF DU PR&Eacute;SENT PR&Eacute;AVIS D&rsquo;APPROVISIONNEMENT
Il ne s&rsquo;agit pas d&rsquo;une demande de soumission ni d&rsquo;une demande de proposition.

Dans le contexte des investissements majeurs annonc&eacute;s par le gouvernement et afin de favoriser un partenariat proactif avec l&rsquo;industrie, CDC diffuse le pr&eacute;sent pr&eacute;avis d&rsquo;approvisionnement (PA) afin d&rsquo;informer les experts-conseils d&rsquo;un contrat &agrave; venir &agrave; diff&eacute;rents emplacements en Colombie-Britannique.

Le pr&eacute;sent PA vise &agrave; permettre aux experts-conseils d&rsquo;&eacute;valuer leur capacit&eacute; et leur int&eacute;r&ecirc;t &agrave; y participer, ainsi que de se pr&eacute;parer ad&eacute;quatement en vue du processus de sollicitation.

Il s&rsquo;agit d&rsquo;un avis pr&eacute;liminaire concernant un contrat potentiel qui comporte des exigences en mati&egrave;re de s&eacute;curit&eacute;. Ce PA vise &agrave; permettre aux experts-conseils qui le souhaitent la possibilit&eacute; d&rsquo;entamer, au besoin, le processus de parrainage afin d&rsquo;obtenir (si n&eacute;cessaire) les habilitations ou les attestations de s&eacute;curit&eacute; requises.

Veuillez noter qu&rsquo;il n&rsquo;y a aucune garantie que ce contrat sera mis de l&rsquo;avant ni que les attestations de s&eacute;curit&eacute; seront accord&eacute;es dans les d&eacute;lais anticip&eacute;s ou seront m&ecirc;me accord&eacute;es dans le cadre du processus de parrainage.

2. Description de l&rsquo;accord d&rsquo;offre permanente et des services

Num&eacute;ro de PA&nbsp;: 88336
Estim&eacute; approximatif&nbsp;: 1&nbsp;000&nbsp;000&nbsp;$
Date de publication pr&eacute;vue&nbsp;: Hiver&nbsp;2027

Description&nbsp;:
Selon leurs politiques, le minist&egrave;re de la D&eacute;fense nationale&nbsp;(MDN) et les Forces arm&eacute;es canadiennes&nbsp;(FAC) doivent maintenir en place un programme de s&eacute;curit&eacute; g&eacute;n&eacute;rale&nbsp;(PGS) en vue de tenir compte des consid&eacute;rations en mati&egrave;re de s&eacute;curit&eacute; dans tous les aspects de leurs op&eacute;rations, de l&rsquo;instruction et de leurs activit&eacute;s de soutien. L&rsquo;expert-conseil sera responsable de dispenser au MDN et aux FAC des cours de formation relevant de la cat&eacute;gorie de la formation sur la s&eacute;curit&eacute; selon les besoins et de les tenir &agrave; jour (s&rsquo;il y a lieu). 3. Exigences &eacute;ventuelles en mati&egrave;re de s&eacute;curit&eacute; et d&rsquo;attribution du contrat
Pour &ecirc;tre admissible &agrave; l&rsquo;attribution d&rsquo;un contrat, un proposant devra, entre autres, d&eacute;tenir toute cote de s&eacute;curit&eacute; requise avant la date de l&rsquo;octroi du contrat, comme il sera indiqu&eacute; en d&eacute;tail dans les documents de la sollicitation.

4. Parrainage dans le cadre du Programme de s&eacute;curit&eacute; industrielle (PSI)
Construction de D&eacute;fense Canada (CDC) offre aux experts-conseils l&rsquo;opportunit&eacute; de se faire parrainer en vue d&rsquo;obtenir une attestation de s&eacute;curit&eacute; par l&rsquo;entremise du Programme de s&eacute;curit&eacute; industrielle (PSI). Par cons&eacute;quent, les experts-conseils qui pr&eacute;voient pr&eacute;senter une proposition pour ce projet et qui ne d&eacute;tiennent pas activement l&rsquo;attestation de s&eacute;curit&eacute; identifi&eacute;e ci-dessus devraient commencer imm&eacute;diatement le processus de demande d&rsquo;attestation de s&eacute;curit&eacute; en faisant la demande par l&rsquo;interm&eacute;diaire du PSI de CDC.

Dans le cadre de ce programme, CDC peut, &agrave; son enti&egrave;re discr&eacute;tion, fournir une aide pr&eacute;liminaire aux proposants pour le processus de parrainage visant l&rsquo;obtention d&rsquo;une attestation de s&eacute;curit&eacute;.

Pour commencer ce processus, veuillez pr&eacute;senter une demande de parrainage &agrave; CDC en suivant les &eacute;tapes suivantes qui se trouvent sur son site Web &agrave;&nbsp;: https://www.cdc-dcc.gc.ca/industrie/exigences-de-s&eacute;curit&eacute;.

Dans la demande de parrainage qu&rsquo;ils pr&eacute;sentent &agrave; CDC, les experts-conseils sont pri&eacute;s de notamment indiquer les renseignements suivants&nbsp;:

	Le num&eacute;ro du pr&eacute;avis d&rsquo;approvisionnement, tel qu&rsquo;indiqu&eacute; &agrave; la section&nbsp;2 de ce PA;
	Le niveau de cote de s&eacute;curit&eacute; demand&eacute; dans le cadre du parrainage, tel qu&rsquo;indiqu&eacute; &agrave; la section&nbsp;3 de ce PA.


5. Processus de parrainage

Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice

This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals.

In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at CFB Shilo, Shilo Manitoba.

The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process, notably by initiating any necessary steps.

This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable).

Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process.

Description of the Project and Services

The Department of National Defence and Defence Construction Canada intends to put in place a contract to provide all labour, material, supervision and equipment to supply janitorial services at CFB Shilo, Manitoba.&nbsp;

In general, the work includes, but not limited to:

Janitorial cleaning services (internal and external elements)

	wipe down benches, exercise equipment and weight machines;

	cleaning and disinfecting of drinking fountains;
	spot clean/ replace of entrance mats and grates;
	floor strip/refinishing;
	sweep/vacuum and damp mop of flooring;
	vacuum (automatic type) pools;
	clean and disinfect pool deck;
	clean, damp mop and disinfect sauna room;
	cleaning and disinfect bathroom fixtures;
	waste removal;
	glass cleaning

Other Tasks


	carpet/furniture shampooing and steam cleaning

The approximate estimated cost for these services is $4,000,000.00 over two (2) years with the potential for three (3) additional one (1) year extensions and an increase in value up to $6,000,000.00. Il ne s&rsquo;agit pas d&rsquo;une demande de soumissions ni d&rsquo;une demande de propositions.

Facilities Maintenance and Support Services
Northern Canada (with Security Requirements)
Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice
This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals.
This is an advance notice for potential contracts with anticipated security requirements to provide interested contractors an opportunity to begin the sponsorship process for obtaining (if required) the anticipated security clearance(s) . Note that there is no guarantee that these solicitation(s) will proceed or that any security clearance(s) will be granted under the sponsorship process in a timely fashion or otherwise.
Description of the Project and Services
The Department of National Defence requires Facilities Maintenance and Support Services for approximately 100 existing buildings and associated utility infrastructure with an approximate total gross floor area of 60,000 m2. In addition to the buildings there are utility services, parking lots, sidewalks, roads and landscaped areas that form part of the site included under the provisions of the project(s).

The site locations are as follows:
Manitoba: Churchill
Northwest Territories: Inuvik, Yellowknife
Yukon: Whitehorse
Nunavut: Eureka, Resolute Bay, Gascoyne Inlet, Nanisivik Naval Facility, Rankin Inlet, Iqaluit,

The services provided by the Contractor may vary based on Sites:&nbsp;All the services listed will have Scheduled and/or &ldquo;On-Demand"" requirements.

	Hard Services



	Building Envelope Maintenance
	Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning &amp; Refrigeration Systems
	Door Systems
	Electrical Systems
	Elevator and Lifting Systems
	Plumbing Systems
	Fire Detection and Suppression Systems
	Generators
	Life Safety Systems
	Security and Access Control Systems
	Kitchen Appliances and Equipment



	Soft Services



	Integrated Pest Management Services
	Landscaping and Grounds Maintenance Services
	Janitorial Services
	Hazardous Waste Management Services
	Environmental Services
	Snow and Ice Control Services
	Solid Waste Management
	Utility Billing Support Services



	Facilities Support Services



	Service Management &amp; Coordination
	Maintenance Program Management
	Emergency Readiness and Response
	Asset Investment Advice
	Help Desk Services

The Contractor(s) will also be required to undertake work that is outside the scope of the scheduled and demand services. This work will be priced, managed and implemented using an Additional Work Request (AWR) process.
The services will be delivered through Facility Maintenance and Support Services (FM) contracts. It is anticipated that one contract will cover locations in Manitoba, the Northwest Territories, and Yukon (Total potential estimated value: $240M), and a separate contract will cover locations in Nunavut (Total potential estimated value: $225M). Each initial contract is expected to have a term of five (5) years, with provisions for two (2) additional option periods of three (3) years each, for a total potential contract duration of up to eleven (11) years.
It is anticipated that these solicitations will be initiated in Winter 2026/2027 timeframe with Service Commencement in Winter 2028.&nbsp; This is conditional on the Project(s) receiving approval to proceed by the Department of National Defence (DND).

The Government of Canada is committed to advancing reconciliation and fostering meaningful engagement with Indigenous Peoples. In alignment with these commitments, the Department of National Defence (DND) seeks to create opportunities for Indigenous businesses and communities through (sub)contracting, employment, and training initiatives associated with the proposed program of work.

It is anticipated that Indigenous communities will benefit from potential subcontracting, employment, and training opportunities arising from this program of work.
Contract Award and Anticipated Security Requirements
To be eligible for contract award, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents.
The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Facility Security Clearance (FSC) at the level of Secret.
Industrial Security Program Sponsorship 
Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors that intend to submit a proposal on one or more of these projects and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC&rsquo;s ISP.
Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential &nbsp;proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process.
To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC&rsquo;s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements.
In their sponsorship request application to DCC, contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things:

	Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number (Project number on the MERX notice);
	Contract number &nbsp;84735&nbsp;; and
	Level of clearance requested to be sponsored for.

Sponsorship Process
Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages.
Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a contractor:

	has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation(s) (Contract number(s) listed on their request for sponsorship) being advertised on MERX,
	has&nbsp; met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package, and
	has submitted a proposal.

DCC will &nbsp;send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada&rsquo;s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP).
Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP &nbsp;to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible.
